summary: Utopia is an interactive web platform that makes NASA's SPHEREx infrared sky survey easy to explore for everyone, from students to researchers. Instead of navigating complex archives, users can search any position or object in the sky and instantly see every SPHEREx image covering it, overlaid with WISE, DSS2, 2MASS and Gaia DR3 data. Utopia's Time Machine lets users play through repeated observations, compare images and detect changes over time, while the Spectral Explorer builds a 0.75–5 µm spectrum and light curve for any target, with proper-motion tracking and CSV export. A change-detection tool flags sources that brightened, dimmed, appeared or disappeared, and presents them as candidates for verification. Utopia turns raw mission data into a visual, scroll-driven experience, making a new space mission accessible, engaging and useful for discovery.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Utopia is a website plus a FastAPI backend that queries NASA/IPAC IRSA for SPHEREx observations and renders cutouts, spectra and difference images. It has five pages:

- Home: a scroll-driven rocket launch with mission facts.

- Sky Explorer: finds every SPHEREx image covering a position or object, with layers for the SPHEREx 102-band cube, WISE, DSS2, 2MASS and a Gaia DR3 overlay.

- Time Machine: plays through observations, compares two images, combines same-band images and detects changes.

- Spectral Explorer: builds a 0.75–5 µm spectrum and light curve of any target. Users can pick detectors and a date range, follow moving targets using proper motion, click a point to see its cutout, and export CSV.

- Discoveries: lists sources flagged by change detection.

HOW IT WORKS

The backend fetches data live from IRSA and VizieR, so new releases (DR1, QR3 and later) appear automatically while superseded releases are hidden. Downloads are parallel, retried and cached in memory and on disk for speed. Change detection finds 5σ sources, compares only images at nearly the same wavelength, and labels each source as brightened, dimmed, variable, appeared, disappeared or stable. It uses plain statistics, so every candidate needs verification.

SCIENTIFIC CARE

We never co-add images from different detectors because they cover different wavelengths. The Spectral Explorer is a quick-look aperture photometry tool, not a replacement for IRSA's Tractor spectrophotometry.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Utopia lowers the barrier to using SPHEREx data. Students, educators and citizen scientists can explore the infrared sky and see how it changes over time, and researchers get a fast way to inspect a target and shortlist variable sources.

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, JavaScript/HTML/CSS frontend, NASA/IPAC IRSA services, VizieR.

CREATIVITY

We combined a cinematic, scroll-driven introduction with real scientific tools in one place, so the same app works for curiosity and for quick-look research.
